messages:
Morgan: quick handoff from me — 03:20UTC incident wrap and current TODOs. Short version: yesterday evening we saw a sudden spike in batcher memory usage in us-west-2 which led to increased 5xx/503s on hosted text-generation routes. We paged SRE and infra; mitigation sequence completed but still monitoring. Full notes below.

Morgan: What happened
- 02:42UTC: router started returning 429/503 for ~10% of requests for /v1/generate (p95 latency up).
- 02:45UTC: paging threshold hit -> page to oncall.
- Root cause: single batcher process on a subset of nodes had KV-cache growth + memory leak while serving long-context jobs. This caused OOM throttles on that pod and upstream 503s.

Morgan: Immediate actions taken
- ops-bot created INCIDENT #234 (see link): https://incidents.redwood.ai/234 :incident:
- Router fallback enabled: route /v1/generate -> model-variant-sm (smaller memory profile) for affected customers (auto-routed, no API key changes).
- Applied soft throttle at ingress for requests > 30k tokens/session to reduce pressure.
- Temporary node cordon + restart of batcher pods on affected ASG.
- Deploy-bot rolled a hotfix to batcher image (gc tuning + kv-ttl) at 03:05UTC.

Morgan: Current status
- 03:30UTC: error rate down from 8% -> 0.6% on affected routes (observed over 10m).
- Router fallback still enabled as safety net.
- Memory telemetry for batchers shows gradual decline; GC pauses improved.
- Customers with high-throughput pipelines (team: embeddings-at-scale) saw degraded latency during peak window. Outreach initiated by Customer Success (CS pinged).

Morgan: Coverage / who is taking what next
- Primary for next shift (03:40-11:40UTC): Tara (will be primary pager).
- Secondary: Sanjay (pager backup + will handle infra escalations).
- On-call for APAC night window: coverage gap noted between 14:00-18:00UTC — no local APAC engineer scheduled. Need to flag to rotations team if increased churn.

Morgan: Runbook pointers (short)
- Runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/batcher-ooms — walkthrough to identify bad pods and safe rollouts.
- Quick commands:
```bash
# list batcher pods with memory usage
kubectl top pods -n inference | grep batcher
# cordon + drain node with bad pod
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-18-123 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-18-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# rollback router config if needed (staging style flag)
redwoodctl router set-fallback --route /v1/generate --variant model-variant-sm --reason "emergency fallback"
```

Morgan: Next steps (assigned)
- Tara: validate that fallback remains healthy and customer-facing errors stay <=1% for next 2 hours. Post a status update at +1h and +2h.
- Sanjay: follow up on the hotfix image rollout across all regions, check CI canary metrics, and prepare a patch-backport if necessary.
- Priya (SRE): coordinate CS outreach summary with affected customers and confirm mitigation satisfied SLAs.
- Devon (infra): open a postmortem ticket and start collecting heap dumps from the affected batcher pods (if still present).

Tara: I took the primary — will start monitoring dashboards now. Checking canary logs and will ping infra if any regressions.

Sanjay: noted. I'll run a cluster-wide check for remaining pods with >70% mem and post the command outputs to this thread if I find candidates.

Priya: CS update queued. We told two impacted customers the timeline and the temporary fallback. They want ETA on full fix — I'll coordinate with infra for an ETA and include it in the customer note.

Devon: started heap collection on the two nodes that still have lingering high mem (jobs started). If heap dump confirms kv growth we'll include that in postmortem.

ops-bot: INCIDENT #234 created by Morgan at 02:52UTC — severity: P2. Pager triggered to oncall rotation group.

deploy-bot: hotfix image redwood/batcher:gc-fix-2026-03 applied to us-west-2 ASG at 03:05UTC. Canary ratio 5% -> 100% in 12m.

Tara: quick note about coverage gap — I'm happy to extend my shift by 2h if needed tonight to cover APAC handoffs. @rotations-team please advise if formal swap needed. :handshake:

Morgan: leaving the thread to Tara — main ask is keep fallback until next check-in and escalate if error rate trends up for two consecutive 10m windows. Short-circuit for any customer-impacting regression by flipping router route back to model-variant-sm permanently for affected API keys.

Tara: will do. I'll post a final handoff summary in ~2 hours with metrics and any outstanding work. :white_check_mark:
